Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

autoSpectra 0.4.0

Redesign around the methodology of Safanelli et al. (2025), a correction that roughly doubles VisNIR accuracy, and a set of safeguards that stop OSSL training data from being redistributed inside published model archives.

Half the training rows had no spectra (fixed)

The OSSL L0 tables carry one row per soil layer, not per scan: a layer with no scan on a given instrument still gets a row, with every spectral column empty. That is 52.4% of the VisNIR table and 36.9% of MIR.

.prepare_preprocessed_matrix() replaced non-finite cells with 0 before the is.finite(rowSums(X)) filter meant to drop those rows, so an all-NA row became an all-zero row, passed the filter, and entered training as a constant vector (constant −1 after SNV). Every such row is identical to every other, so identical inputs force identical predictions and impose a hard, model-independent ceiling on test R².

That ceiling, not the models, was the binding constraint:

property ceiling measured (VAE) Safanelli
oc 0.513 0.459 0.78
n.tot 0.508 0.446 0.81
ph.h2o 0.462 0.381 0.50
clay.tot 0.302 0.229 0.25

Safanelli’s oc and n.tot figures sat above our ceiling — unreachable by arithmetic rather than by modelling. The bug also explains two things that never made sense: why a masked VAE and Cubist+PCA landed within 0.05 of each other on every property (the limit was upstream of both), and why clay.tot appeared to be “at parity” (its ceiling is 0.302 because 66% of its rows were blank — a coincidence of censoring, not evidence that VisNIR carries no clay signal).

has_spectral_coverage() now runs before the zero-fill. Partial coverage is still kept, since that is exactly what the masked soilVAE exists to handle; only rows with no coverage at all are dropped. VisNIR oc went from R² 0.459 to 0.850 (RMSE 8.478 → 4.824, CCC 0.601 → 0.906), above the Safanelli baseline of 0.78 / 5.27 / 0.82.

Any model or Zenodo archive built before this fix is invalid and must be regenerated.

Data provenance and redistribution (read this before republishing to Zenodo)

Model archives built by earlier versions of upload_models.R embedded the OSSL training database inside the Cubist bundles, by two independent routes:

  • pca$scores — the 120 PCA coordinates of every training sample (105,992 x 120 for MIR). Since the same file also carried pca$rotation and pca$center, .reconstruct_pca() inverted them back to the input spectra at 100% of the retained variance.
  • model$data — Cubist::cubist() retains a verbatim CSV copy of the entire training matrix, predictors and response, in this slot. For OSSL_MIR_Cubist/oc that was 307,275,015 bytes: one line per OSSL sample, carrying both the PC scores and the laboratory value in plain text.

OSSL v1.2 is CC-BY 4.0, so redistribution with attribution is permitted and no licence was breached. The problem is that a file published as a model silently contained a copy of the source database, and nothing in the pipeline objected. Across 16 bundles this was 1,005.9 MB of payload where 12.7 MB was intended.

Neither slot is read at prediction time, so removing them changes nothing: .project_pca() uses only rotation/center/scale, and Cubist predictions are bit-identical without $data (verified on all 8 bundles).

Three layers now prevent this:

  • Write side — .strip_pca_scores() and .strip_cubist_data() are applied to the response model and the conformal error model before saveRDS(). pca$n_train is kept as a provenance count.
  • Publish side — upload_models.R now ships by allowlist (.PUBLISHABLE_PATTERNS) instead of by denylist, and refuses to build an archive containing an unrecognised file. The previous denylist excluded only *.log and *.tmp, matched nothing in the repository, and would have shipped the leak without complaint.
  • Verify side — audit_release_archive() opens a built zip and inspects every artefact, failing on any file outside the allowlist, any array with a per-sample axis, or any character blob containing delimited numeric records. upload_models.R runs it automatically and deletes any archive that fails.

ossl_download_file() remains the only way OSSL data enters the package: it is fetched at run time from the official bucket documented at https://docs.soilspectroscopy.org/db-access.html into a user-local cache, and is never bundled or re-hosted.

New: four model families

Two algorithms across two spectral domains, all sharing the same preprocessing, target transforms, validation strategy and applicability-domain machinery:

  • OSSL_VisNIR, OSSL_MIR — masked soilVAE. A two-channel [SNV spectrum | coverage mask] input with a masked-MSE reconstruction loss, trained with spectral_dropout() augmentation that simulates partial-coverage instruments, so prediction does not depend on a specific band range.
  • OSSL_VisNIR_Cubist, OSSL_MIR_Cubist — a faithful replication of the Safanelli et al. (2025) reference pipeline: SNV, PCA(120), Cubist with committee tuning by inner 5-fold CV, Q-statistic applicability domain (Jackson–Mudholkar, 99%), and normalised conformal prediction at 68%.

Improvements

  • Metrics are reported in the original units. Properties trained under log1p are back-transformed with expm1() before scoring, so RMSE, R², RPIQ and CCC are directly comparable with Safanelli’s Tables 4 and 5.
  • .fit_pca() uses irlba::prcomp_irlba() for large matrices — a randomised truncated SVD that is far cheaper in memory and time than a full prcomp() at rank 120 on a 130k x 1076 matrix.
  • Training is resumable. A property counts as finished only when both its model and its _metrics.json exist, so an interrupted run continues from the next unfinished property; --force retrains regardless.
  • keras3::clear_session() and gc() run between properties. Without them, accumulated backend state aborted the process while building the second model of a run (condition_variable wait failed on macOS).
  • Spectral ranges follow Safanelli: VisNIR 350–2500 nm (1,076 bands), MIR 600–4000 cm⁻¹ (1,701 bands).

Bug fixes

  • keras3::save_model() is called with overwrite = TRUE. Without it a re-run trained each property for its full epoch budget and then discarded the result with “File already exists” — a failure that only surfaced after the expensive part.
  • An interrupted OSSL download no longer masquerades as a valid cache. Downloads land on a .part path and are renamed only after the HTTP status and the gzip stream both verify. Note that R’s gzfile() cannot detect this: it reads a truncated member up to the cut and reports a clean EOF, so the CRC32/ISIZE trailer is checked with gzip -t.
  • split_idx() used sampled values as negative indices instead of positions, which overlapped the train and test sets.
  • upload_models.R evaluated normalizePath(MODEL_DIR) after setwd(MODEL_DIR), resolving a nonexistent models/models; the archive path prefix was stripped correctly only by accident.
  • Migrated to keras3 and the .keras model format.

Testing

129 tests. New coverage for the redistribution guards, the release auditor (including planted-leak red-team cases and the false-positive cases that a size-based check got wrong), OSSL cache integrity, the save/overwrite/load round-trip for models carrying custom Sampling and masked_mse objects, and the PCA and conformal paths.
